children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were stepping back Friday morning, continuing the losses from the overnight session.
The Chicago soy complex was to the downside, along with Malaysian palm oil and most European rapeseed contracts. Crude oil was mixed, which provided little direction to the vegetable oils.

Saskatchewan reported its canola harvest reached 15% complete. Due to wet conditions during the reporting week, the overall provincial harvest nudged a mere five points to 32% finished, 39 points behind the five-year average.
Prairie temperatures have been forecast to push into the low 20 degrees Celsius Friday with sunny skies across the region, except for southern Manitoba which is to get rain.

There was a negligible amount of canola exports for the week ended Sept. 13, according to the Canadian Grain Commission. The year-to-date nudged up to 709,600 tonnes. Domestic use was relatively steady on the week at 237,800 tonnes with the cumulative total just short of 1.55 million tonnes.
Canola crush margins contracted, with the November positions down by more than C$6 between C$269.10 and C$276.15 per tonne above the futures.
The Canadian dollar eased back Friday morning with the loonie at 71.42 U.S. cents, compared with Thursday's close of 71.49.
About 11,400 contracts had been traded by 9:39 a.m. ET and prices in Canadian dollars per metric tonne were:
